- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates in the first 5–7 days of a new 30-day forecast horizon; apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias for early days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.20) and history shows mean reversion, model often fails to recognize it; apply a 0.3–0.7% downward bias to align with historical mean.
- If sentiment spikes to 1.00 (strong bullish), model often overreacts; cap forecast at 1.5–2.0% above recent high, then adjust downward if sentiment cools.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment when it’s flat (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days; if sentiment remains flat, apply a 0.2–0.5% downward bias to avoid false optimism.
